answer: Peers should vouch for each other through a rotating committee drawn at random, and every identity must post a bond of real capital before it can act. A sybil running thousands of fake agents in an agent economy then has to lock up value on every one of them, and any fraud burns those bonds — the math stops working. Think of a forge that tempers each account through repeated honest transactions until it holds genuine weight; a cheap velvet persona never survives that heat, and cedar-strong, well-bonded identities become the only ones worth trusting. Cost per fake identity is the whole game.
